Home / Services / Electronics and firmware design

Design and development

Electronics and firmware design, from an idea to a working prototype.

We design the circuit boards and the software that runs on them, and build prototypes you can test, show to investors or put in front of your first customers. You don't need a technical specification to start — we help you write one.

Send an inquiry

Designing a device means getting many decisions right at once: which components to use, how the board is laid out, how the firmware behaves, how the device talks to phones, apps or the internet, and how it will later be produced and tested. We handle all of these together, so the prototype is not just a demo but a sound starting point for production.

Already have an engineering team? We can join for the parts that need extra hands or specialist experience, working with your tools and processes.

What you get

  • Requirements and technical specification
  • Electronics and PCB design
  • Embedded software (firmware)
  • Connection to phones, apps and the cloud
  • Working prototypes
  • All design files, code and documentation handed over

When it helps

  • You have an idea for a device but no in-house electronics team.
  • Your team needs help with a difficult part of the design.
  • An existing device needs a redesign, for example because a part is no longer available.

How it works

From the first call to the result.

  1. Requirements

    We work out together what the device must do, where it will be used and what it may cost to make.

  2. Design

    Component choice, schematics, circuit board layout and the structure of the software.

  3. Prototype

    A working prototype you can test and show. We fix whatever the tests reveal.

  4. Ready for production

    Design files, firmware and documentation prepared so the device can be built and tested in series.

FAQ

Common questions

Do I need a technical specification?

No. A sketch or a short description is enough. We turn it into clear requirements and a plan before anything is built.

Who owns the design?

You do. All schematics, circuit board files, source code and documentation are handed over to you.

How long does a prototype take?

It depends on the device. After the first call you receive a written plan with stages, dates and a price for each stage.

Tell us about your project.

Describe the problem or product and where you are now — a rough description is fine. We reply within two working days, and the first call is free.
